title: Compute mean length-at-age — get_growth
text: Uses Schnute parameterization von Bertalanffy growth curve, $$L_a = L_1 + (L_2 - L_1)\frac{1 - e^{-k(- A_1)}}{1 - e^{-k(A_2 - A_1)}}.$$ Optionally reproduces SS3 GrowthModel 3 (age-specific K), including cumulative multipliers plus-group approximation. Multipliers apply cumulatively: K age base K times product multipliers ages less equal . final K carries forward. Linf derived L1, L2, A1 A2 using oldest-age K; growth age +1 uses K . Consequently, multipliers curve need pass L2 A2. A1 must modeled age option. A1, opal retains base-K exponential growth toward Linf; SS3 instead uses linear segment. plus-group approximation averages linear increase oldest length Linf max_age ages, weights exp(-0.2)^j, j = 0, ..., max_age. fixed 0.2 mortality; option requires positive integer oldest age. log_k log rate per model age unit, whereas SS3 reads annual rate scales season duration. quarterly age step, use log(K_SS3 * 3/12); multipliers dimensionless. reimplementation pinned SS3 v3.24AB beginning--season lengths; later SS3 versions may differ. title: Compute mean length-at-age — get_growth
text: Uses Richards (1959) curve parameterized Schnute (1981), $$L_a = \left[L_1^b + (L_2^b - L_1^b)\frac{1 - e^{-k(- A_1)}}{1 - e^{-k(A_2 - A_1)}}\right]^{1/b}.$$ parameterization guidance subsection follow Stock Synthesis user manual (section 8.5.2.2.2, Richards growth function). See Richards growth vignette Stock Synthesis website technical guidance. b = 1 gives VB curve. b approaches 0, curve approaches Gompertz curve; Gompertz growth can obtained fixing b small value 1e-4. b floating-point parameter natural scale may positive negative exactly 0. initial value non-zero, effectively risk estimated b landing exactly 0. A1 greater youngest modeled age, parameter combinations give undefined (NaN) predicted lengths younger ages. A1 fraction equation negative, b > 0 bracket can become negative. b < 0 asymptotic bracket can zero negative, case Linf undefined. choice A1 A2 also constrains possible curve shapes. opal clamp bracket.

title: Compute mean length-at-age — get_growth
text: Uses growth cessation model Maunder et al. (2018), Eq. 2, $$L_t = L_0 + r_{max}\left[\frac{\ln(e^{-k t_{50}} + 1) - \ln(e^{k(t - t_{50})} + 1)}{k} + t\right],$$ rmax = exp(log_rmax) k = exp(log_k_gc). growth rate declines logistically rmax, midpoint age t50. L(0) = L0, asymptotic length \(L_0 + r_{max}[\ln(e^{-k t_{50}} + 1)/k + t_{50}]\). k approaches 0, curve approaches L0 + rmax * t / 2. log terms computed overflow-safe \(\log(1 + e^x)\) (RTMB::logspace_add AD inputs), avoids overflow large k * (t - t50). Unlike VB Richards curves, depend - A1, curve depends absolute age t, age origin matters. t modeled age plus age_offset. example, model age 1 corresponds biological age 0, use age_offset = -1.

title: Double Richards selectivity as a function of length — sel_double_richards
text: smooth, six-parameter curve formed multiplying ascending generalized-logistic (Richards) limb one minus descending Richards limb: $$(1 + \exp(-z_1))^{-1/\gamma_1} [1 - (1 + \exp(-z_2))^{-1/\gamma_2}].$$ Parameters real line transformed follows: par[1] Ascending 50% point: mean(len) + par[1] * sd(len). par[2] Ascending width: exp(par[2]) * sd(len). par[3] Ascending shape: gamma1 = exp(par[3]). par[4] Descending 50% point ascending 50% point plus exp(par[4]) * sd(len). par[5] Descending width: exp(par[5]) * sd(len). par[6] Descending shape: gamma2 = exp(par[6]). Maunder parameterization recovered alpha_k = L50_k + log(2^gamma_k - 1) / beta_k beta_k = log(19) / width_k. peak can one limbs overlap; intentionally rescaled. either shape parameter tends negative infinity, limb tends Gompertz curve 50% point. Large shape values flatten limb toward 0.5 (par[3] = par[6] = 7, curve approximately 0.25). Mapping par[3] par[6] zero gives four-parameter double-logistic curve. CPUE data: cpue_switch Indicator CPUE inclusion (1 = included, typically fishery 15). n_index Number distinct CPUE/survey indices (integer). cpue_data Tibble 268 rows 9 columns containing standardized CPUE observations: year: Calendar year (1952-2018) month: Quarter month (2, 5, 8, 11 Q1-Q4) ts: Sequential timestep (1-268) fishery: Fleet identifier (usually 15 survey fleet) index: Integer index identifier (1, 2, ..., n_index) metric: Data type ("cpue") units: Unit code (typically 2 fishery 15) value: Normalized CPUE observations se: Log-space standard error CPUE observations Biological parameters: lw_a Length-weight allometric coefficient (6.48e-05). lw_b Length-weight allometric exponent (2.78). maturity Maturity length vector (95 elements). Ogive-based maturity probabilities length bin. fecundity Fecundity length vector (95 elements). Relative fecundity length bin. M Natural mortality age vector (40 elements). Age-specific instantaneous mortality rates. Age bounds: A1 Minimum age credibility interval (1). A2 Maximum age credibility interval (40). Selectivity: sel_type_f Selectivity function type fishery (15 elements). Integer codes representing selectivity curve shapes: 1 = logistic, 2 = double-normal, 3 = double Richards. Curves evaluated length; optional sel_basis_f data element (1 = length, 2 = age) evaluates age instead (see get_selectivity()). Priors: priors List 8 Bayesian prior specifications, containing: type: Prior distribution type ("normal", etc.) par1: First parameter (mean location) par2: Second parameter (std dev scale) index: Parameter index model Priors cover: log_B0, log_cpue_q, par_sel, log_L1, log_L2, log_k, log_CV1, log_CV2. Length composition data: lf_minbin Integer vector (n_fishery). Per-fishery minimum bin index lower-tail aggregation. Bins 1 lf_minbin[f] summed bin lf_minbin[f]. Default 1 (aggregation). lf_maxbin Integer vector (n_fishery). Per-fishery maximum bin index upper-tail aggregation. Bins lf_maxbin[f] n_len summed bin lf_maxbin[f]. Default n_len (aggregation).
